routes.description: Establish that the precise and predictive applicability of independently developed mathematics is a genuine explanatory datum, remains contingent under naturalism, and is expected if a divine mind intentionally gives the physical world mathematical structure.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds by preserving the surprising applicability datum against practical-development, approximation, and selection-effect objections, then showing that intentional divine construction supplies a deeper comparative explanation than naturalistic necessity.

motionBridge.description: Connect the surprising applicability of mathematics to an intentional divine ordering of creation and show why that connection supports theism better than naturalism.

centralBridges.description: Establish that mathematics developed by a priori standards nevertheless describes and predicts physical phenomena with accuracy that calls for explanation.
Show that provisional theories, approximate truth, non-instantiable mathematical structures, and unsuccessful applications do not dissolve the relevant explanatory datum.
Explain how divine conception and intentional creation can produce a world structured according to mathematics under either realist or anti-realist mathematical ontology.

Maintain that a nonexistent, chaotic, or mathematically inaccessible physical reality is metaphysically possible, so mathematical order cannot be explained merely by postulated naturalistic necessity.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Clarify the role of mathematical fruitfulness and richness in supporting sufficient independence from anticipated empirical application.
Distinguish an explanatory appeal to divine free choice from a bare restatement that mathematical structure or applicability is necessary.

routes.description: Challenge whether mathematical applicability is as independent, accurate, and selectively successful as alleged, then provide a naturalistic modal account on which mathematically formulable laws and boundary conditions are necessary rather than an unexplained coincidence.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds by undermining the claimed need for a distinctively theistic explanation or by showing that an independently motivated naturalistic necessity account explains the datum while divine freedom introduces an equivalent or deeper explanatory stopping point.

motionBridge.description: Show that naturalism can accommodate mathematical applicability without brute coincidence and that theism supplies no superior comparative explanation.

centralBridges.description: Contest the alleged unexpectedness of applicability by examining problem-driven mathematical development, false yet predictive theories, discarded solutions, and failed predictions.
Require a coherent account of how approximate, structurally inaccurate, or non-instantiable mathematics relates to the physical world before its success supports a metaphysical inference.
Derive mathematical applicability from a naturalistic cosmology whose laws and boundary conditions necessarily admit mathematical formulation.
Determine whether God could create a world lacking mathematical applicability and show how either necessity or brute divine choice affects the claimed explanatory advantage.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Separate truth-directed mathematical problem solving from aesthetic motivation without assuming that scientific utility directly drives mathematical research.
Frame modal necessity as part of an independently developed total metaphysical theory assessed through explanatory scope and economy.

sections.title: Unexpectedness and the Development of Mathematics
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether mathematics is sufficiently independent of physical inquiry, yet sufficiently accurate in application, to generate the initial explanatory burden on which the comparative argument depends.

sections.title: Truth, Approximation, and Physical Structure
sections.rationale: The relation between successful mathematical theories and actual physical structure matters because predictive accuracy can support the motion only if provisional or false theories still instantiate the relevant explanatory phenomenon.

sections.title: Instantiation and Nonphysical Mathematical Resources
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether physical structural instantiation exhausts the applicability datum or whether indispensable non-instantiable resources create an additional burden for both theistic and naturalistic explanations.

sections.title: Failed Applications and Selection Effects
sections.rationale: The balance between striking successes and numerous discarded solutions or failed predictions determines whether observed applicability is genuinely anomalous or partly produced by selective attention.

sections.title: Naturalistic Necessity and Modal Contingency
sections.rationale: This is a principal motion-level clash because the naturalistic rival depends on necessary mathematical order, while the theistic route depends on that order being contingent and intentionally selected.

sections.title: Divine Freedom and Explanatory Depth
sections.rationale: The dispute over necessary structure, free divine choice, brute stopping points, and independent theoretical motivation determines whether either worldview provides the deeper comparative explanation required by the motion.
